compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
Today one logical Jira update can pass through generic apply retry, Cloud ACLI or REST retry, Jira DC SDK retry, and recovery reads. Persistent faults can multiply wire calls; late failure can replay already-successful substeps; long `Retry-After` values can be capped and retried early. The coordinator needs a proven vertical contract before migrating every operation.

## Outcome
Route one representative issue-update postcondition end to end for Jira Cloud and Jira DC through typed provider-neutral outcomes and one immutable retry budget. The concrete adapter owns physical execution, timeout/cleanup, provider decoding, and hidden SDK retry disablement. The budget covers the initial call, any safe recovery observation, and replanned call together.

## Plan
1. Add provider-neutral operation outcome/error metadata: logical operation id, atomic postcondition, physical attempt, terminal disposition, normalized scope, replay safety, provider delay, `retry_not_before`, and redacted diagnostics.
2. Add one budget owner with at most three physical invocations and 15 seconds cumulative sleep. Fallback is approximately 2s then 4s plus nonnegative deterministic-injected jitter; provider delay is a lower bound.
3. Adapt one Cloud update route and one DC update route. Disable nested client/SDK retry for those routes, set explicit timeouts, preserve ACLI child reaping, and classify TLS/auth/permanent 4xx without retry.
4. On ambiguous write timeout, observe the atomic postcondition before any replay. A satisfied observation returns recovered success; remaining drift may replan only within the same budget.
5. If an authoritative delay cannot fit, return deferred `retry_not_before` without sleeping early or consuming a fictional attempt.

## Testing (RED → GREEN)
- Deterministic fake ACLI plus a local HTTP server exercise Cloud REST/DC responses, disconnects, timeouts, 429/503, malformed delays, TLS/auth/permanent 4xx, and ambiguous commit.
- A fake clock and injected jitter assert exact attempt/sleep/deadline accounting and zero real sleep.
- Wire-call counters prove no nested retry; process fixtures prove every ACLI timeout terminates/reaps the child.
- Existing provider error/output tests pin redaction and current intentional fast-fail behavior.

## Coordination / portability
Implement after RP-04 S2/S3 have made runtime/backend construction authoritative; record soft relations rather than a promoted whole-epic blocker. All mandatory tests run locally with fake process/HTTP transports and no CI-provider feature or live credential. Optional bounded live probes may add evidence but are never the acceptance oracle.

## Compatibility / rollback
Only the selected update route uses the new executor during expand. A route flag can return it to legacy dispatch before later cutover; it never dual-sends. Rollback retains successful remote effects and re-observes ambiguous ones. This intentionally replaces nested retries and early capped-provider-delay replay for the migrated route.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cloud and DC update fixtures expose one provider-neutral outcome contract with redacted provider metadata and a stable logical operation id.
- [ ] No logical postcondition exceeds three physical invocations or 15 seconds cumulative sleep, including observation/replan; wire counters prove nested SDK/generic retry is disabled.
- [ ] A provider delay is treated as a lower bound; when it cannot fit, the operation returns `retry_not_before` and performs no early replay.
- [ ] TLS, credential, invalid request, permission, and other permanent classifications fast-fail; eligible network/429/5xx outcomes use injected backoff/jitter.
- [ ] Ambiguous update timeout re-observes once, returns recovered success when satisfied, and replays only remaining drift within the same budget.
- [ ] ACLI timeout tests prove process termination/reaping, and all mandatory validation runs against local deterministic transports without external credentials.
